label: CTI
rationale: A chamber-jazz summit built around one of the great long-form performances in the canon's era: Hall's 19-minute reading of Rodrigo's Concierto de Aranjuez with a sextet of Paul Desmond, Chet Baker, Roland Hanna, Ron Carter and Steve Gadd, arranged and conducted by Don Sebesky, recorded over two April 1975 sessions at Van Gelder's. The session-gravity signal is close to maximal - five leaders' worth of players on one date - and AllMusic's review calls it 'one of the highest profile lineups ever put to tape' while ranking it among the best albums of Hall's catalog (S2). Critical standing recorded by Wikipedia: AllMusic 4.5 stars, The Rolling Stone Jazz Record Guide 4 stars (S1); AllMusic files it under Cool, Post-Bop and Guitar Jazz (S2). Discovery value is the argument: a listener sent here cold hears the cool-jazz lineage of Desmond and Hall extended into a 1970s studio setting without a backbeat or an electric instrument in sight. Window note: 1975 sits inside 1945-1985, and this is a 1973+ arrival, so the continuity question (does it extend the post-bebop/modal lineage rather than found something new?) is the one to put to John - the council's call, not mine.

personnel_record.notes: Two sessions at the same room: 16 April 1975 ('The Answer Is Yes', 'Concierto de Aranjuez') and 23 April 1975 ('You'd Be So Nice to Come Home To', 'Two's Blues') per Wikipedia's session note (S1); AllMusic gives both dates and the location (S2) and Discogs says simply 'recorded at Van Gelder Studios in April 1975' (S3). Session-to-track assignment is marked inf because Wikipedia states it by CD numbering, not by title. All sources give album-level personnel only - no per-track exclusions are documented, so track personnel lists the full sextet as inf and track_assignments_complete is false. Durations vary by a few seconds between Wikipedia (7:08 / 3:51 / 7:41 / 19:22) and Discogs (7:04 / 3:48 / 7:36 / 19:17); the Wikipedia timings are recorded here. Only the original four-track LP programme is recorded; the 1997 and later CD editions add 'Rock Skippin'', 'Unfinished Business' and three alternate takes. Don Sebesky is arranger and conductor (S1, S2, S3) and is credited in notes rather than as an instrument; he is not a performing musician on the date.

scope_check.boundary_note: The 1973–1985 continuity test applies: does this CTI chamber-jazz production extend cool and post-bop traditions rather than represent crossover drift? Both references judge the continuity convincing; neither identifies a prohibited style.

ballot.case_for: Concierto offers exceptional session gravity: Hall, Paul Desmond, Chet Baker, Roland Hanna, Ron Carter, and Steve Gadd connect overlapping cool and post-bop traditions in a single leader date (S1–S3). The 19-minute Rodrigo adaptation gives that ensemble a substantial focal point and makes a persuasive discovery vehicle for Hall's lyrical, conversational approach. AllMusic places it among Hall's best albums and praises its unusually distinguished lineup; the dossier also reports favorable AllMusic and Rolling Stone Jazz Record Guide ratings (S1–S2). Its strongest claim is therefore a major Hall statement that carries an established jazz language into 1975, not merely an attractive CTI production.
ballot.case_against: The dossier establishes favorable reception more securely than canonical consensus: it supplies no independent core-list placements or documented musician testimony, and most sources establish metadata rather than artistic importance. Nor does it demonstrate that this album fixed Hall's language or materially shaped subsequent practice; distinguished personnel cannot establish those claims by themselves. A skeptic can hear the polished, classical-derived chamber setting as an exquisite consolidation of established cool-jazz resources rather than a load-bearing development, leaving its necessity to this canon less certain than its quality.
ballot.disagreement: Reference 1 assigns contested because limited consensus and unproven downstream influence leave substantive reservations; Reference 2 assigns scope_call chiefly to honor the post-1973 continuity review. Both agree on strong priority and convincing stylistic continuity, but Reference 2 calls the album a universally recognized defining leader statement and CTI landmark more confidently than Reference 1 or the supplied sources support.
ballot.recommendation: The council proposes that John give Concierto strong-priority listening and adjudicate its post-1973 continuity alongside whether its stature as a Hall leader date outweighs the limited documented consensus.
